name: Material Possessions
overview: Scripture teaches that believers should not place their trust in earthly wealth, which is temporary and vulnerable to decay and theft, but rather prioritize seeking God's kingdom and righteousness, trusting that their needs will be met (Matthew 6:19, 6:33). The Bible warns against serving both God and material wealth, emphasizing that one cannot truly devote oneself to both (Matthew 6:24). True life is not measured by the abundance of possessions, and believers are encouraged to be generous, storing up eternal treasures rather than earthly ones (Luke 12:15, 12:33). Ultimately, gaining the world at the cost of one's soul is a loss far too great, highlighting the eternal value of spiritual well-being over material gain (Matthew 16:26).
